title: ID, repeaters and third-party rules
blurb: When to give your call sign, who's responsible for a repeater's output, and the rules for talking on behalf of others.

T1F01.why: Your station and records must be open to an FCC representative **at any time on request**.
T1F01.trap: No waiting period, written notice or warrant is required.

T1F02.why: A tactical call isn't a call sign. You still give your own call **every 10 minutes and at the end**.

T1F03.why: Identify **at least every 10 minutes during a contact, and at the end**.
T1F03.trap: Not at the start only, not every 15 minutes, and not every transmission.

T1F04.trap: Other languages aren't allowed for a phone ID, even if recognized by the ITU.

T1F05.why: A phone station may send its call sign by **voice or by CW**.

T1F06.why: Slash, stroke and slant are all accepted spoken forms of the "/" in a call sign indicator.

T1F07.why: Talking to a foreign station on behalf of an unlicensed person needs a **third-party agreement** with that country.
T1F07.trap: Citizenship isn't required, and there is no special ID rule for third-party contacts.

T1F08.why: Third-party communication is a message passed **between control operators on behalf of another person**.
T1F08.trap: It isn't "three stations": the "third party" is the person being spoken for.

T1F09.why: A **repeater** retransmits another station's signal on a different channel.

T1F10.why: The **originating station's control operator** is accountable, not the repeater's owner or its control operator.

T1F11.why: A club station license needs a **trustee** and **at least four members**.
T1F11.trap: The trustee doesn't need an Extra, and ARRL registration isn't required.
